content.text:
<document id=DOC_req_years_eight>
Required: 8 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_no_dates>
Backend engineering across transactional services, most recently a
settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day. Previously worked on
payment reconciliation and inventory systems.
</document>

Rewrite the candidate summary below to match the posting requirement.

If years of experience are neither stated nor calculable, ask me for the
figure and tell me what it costs not to supply it.

response.text:
**I need one figure from you: how many years of backend engineering experience do you have?**

The summary has no dates, durations, or start years, so I can't calculate it. The posting lists 8 years as a *required* qualification, so I won't guess or imply a number.

**What it costs to leave it out:**
- **Automated screening:** Applicant tracking systems often filter on an explicit years figure. Without one, the résumé may never reach a person.
- **Recruiter skim:** A reviewer checking "8 years?" in a few seconds will find no answer. Most will assume you fall short rather than dig.
- **No direct match:** The summary can show relevant work but can't claim to meet the requirement, which is the posting's only stated hard criterion.

**Draft with a placeholder** (swap in your number):

> Backend engineer with **[X] years** of experience building transactional services. Most recently built and operated a settlement pipeline processing 40,000 orders per day. Prior backend work spans payment reconciliation and inventory systems, giving end-to-end depth across the order-to-cash lifecycle.

**If your number is 8 or more,** state it exactly as above.
**If it's under 8,** tell me. I'll rework the summary to lead with scale and domain depth instead, and I won't round up or blur the figure.
